<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via assertAppAutomationAppendOnlyWriteAllowed (symbol, a top-level function), registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const), HookSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const), HookSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f97a2d9a040794173b82c21dd13f10ead5e6133c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1f653ed3c5bc06314a9525335e9b7cd8513ff2db` — the merge of head `7db6b8549d48d5846bdfb4060c64dd9d4981c864` into base `f97a2d9a040794173b82c21dd13f10ead5e6133c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1f653ed3c5bc06314a9525335e9b7cd8513ff2db && git checkout 1f653ed3c5bc06314a9525335e9b7cd8513ff2db
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f97a2d9a040794173b82c21dd13f10ead5e6133c 7db6b8549d48d5846bdfb4060c64dd9d4981c864 && git checkout -B drift-repro f97a2d9a040794173b82c21dd13f10ead5e6133c && git merge --no-ff 7db6b8549d48d5846bdfb4060c64dd9d4981c864

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f97a2d9a040794173b82c21dd13f10ead5e6133c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f97a2d9a040794173b82c21dd13f10ead5e6133c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f3347e2adc63bc532af963c026f7f382102a5bfd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-automation-identity-write-refusal.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/runas-system-append-only-write-refusal.integration.test.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-secrets-and-routing.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-middleware-and-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/core/src/security/app-automation-elevation.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/system-write-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signer.ts, packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-job/src/db-job-adapter.ts (cited code read at the head, never reviewed); prose faces read for their claims: .changeset/app-automation-append-only-write-refusal.md, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx row 25, the two regenerated flow reference pages

### ① Derived judgments

- **Verb set.** The refused set (update, transfer, delete, purge, restore) is the data middleware's own non-insert write vocabulary. Insert is absent, as the partial landing intends. For a sandboxed body or the action facade, no further engine write verb reaches storage past the middleware.
- **Predicate.** The check shares one predicate with the identity refusal, read at the same point, ahead of the system short-circuit. No earlier return in the middleware precedes it.
- **Code and status.** The refusal uses the identity refusal's error class: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403.
- **Bucket source.** `managedBy` is read off the live registry on every call; there is no name list. At the head this covers the three audit-seal ledgers as well as the eight older ones.
- **Registry cannot answer.** A name the registry does not resolve passes this check. The engine's own name resolution reads the same registry and refuses the write as not-found, so nothing lands. A host engine without the schema member passes open (nit N2).
- **Platform writers.** Each one read writes under a system context of its own, with no run and no mark. The audit writer, under an automation's write, only inserts. No over-refusal was found among them.
- **Cross-organization.** The refusal is object-level and comes before any row read, so another organization's row gets the same answer and no existence signal. The flow test pins both organizations.
- **Checks.** All check-runs on this head are complete and green.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/spec` is correct under the repo rule. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing…)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and an ADR-0087 not-required marker. The declaration lines in the body and the changeset agree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Insert half.** No published face claims it; see S3 for the lead-in wording.
- **Publish-time lint.** The PR body states it is absent, and no face claims it.
- **Referential clean-up leg.** See M1.
- **An elevated route outside the predicate.** See S1: [detail held by the security seat].

### ④ Design judgment

The direct half makes the ruling's change/delete refusal real and takes away nothing the platform's own writers hold. It does take away one capability it does not declare (M1).

**must-fix**

- **M1. The changeset under-declares the narrowing.**
  - An elevated automation's delete of an ordinary row that a ledger row references is now refused whole. The engine's reference clean-up on the ledger row runs under the automation's context and is judged as the automation's write.
  - The module docblock and the PR body's acceptance note say so. The changeset says the opposite: it lists "its writes to every other object" as unchanged.
  - The remedy sentence does not fit an author who wrote only a delete of their own row.
  - No test pins this leg.
  - Fix: declare it, pin it, and give it a fitting message. Or take to the seat the question of whether that clean-up is the automation's write.

**should-fix**

- **S1. One in-process route for an app-authored hook is outside the predicate:** [detail held by the security seat]. The identity refusal shares this route, so this PR did not introduce it. Narrow the changeset's hook sentence to the routes that are enforced, or close the route under a seat card.
- **S2. The hook and action describes are silent.** The rule is enforced for hooks and action bodies, but only the flow `runAs` describe states it.
- **S3. Lead-in wording.** No published face says that an elevated insert into a ledger is still admitted. Add one clause so the partial landing describes itself. The refusal message needs the same.
- **S4. Row 1b of system-context.mdx** still calls the identity refusal "the one check ahead of the middleware's short-circuit", but row 25 now names a second.

**nit**

- **N1.** Neither row 25's Symbol cell nor the page's symbol register cites the new assertion.
- **N2.** A host engine without the schema member passes the check open (test doubles only).

### ① Derived judgments

It no longer says every elevated hook write fails. The route outside the predicate is unchanged and predates this PR: [detail held by the security seat].
- **S2 — closed.** The hook `runAs` and action `body` descriptions state the rule, its five verbs and that an insert is not judged. The reference pages are regenerated from them.
- **S3 — closed.** The flow description, the source comment, the module docblock, both refusal messages, the changeset and row 25 each say the check covers the five verbs and does not judge an insert.
- **S4 — closed.** Row 1b now says it is checked beside the append-only refusal, and no longer calls itself the one check ahead of the short-circuit.
- **N1 — accepted deviation.** Row 25's Symbol cell cites the shared elevation read site, and the register keys that site to rows 1b and 25. The row's prose names the new assertion. This is the right delivery: the new assertion holds no elevation read of its own, so the read it relies on is the true anchor, and the shrink-only ledger is left alone.
- **N2 — unchanged.** Still a nit, limited to test doubles.
- **Check-runs on this head.** 59 success, 12 skipped, none failed. One second `Check Changeset` run was still in progress when read, started after the PR body was replaced; its first run on this head succeeded.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still correct: `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/spec`, with the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing…)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the ADR-0087 not-required marker. The delta adds description strings and regenerated pages to spec, and no key, value or requirement.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Rule level.** The new public text names the rule, the verbs, the sources and the remedy. The clean-up refusal names an object and a field, never a row. The engine's internal marker for the clean-up leg appears only in source comments.

- **Lint and insert.** Both stated as held for the seat; neither is claimed.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing now declares all of what it takes away: the direct change or delete of a ledger row, and the delete of a record a ledger row references. Both make the ruling's refusal real at the consumer and leave the platform's own writers as they were. Recognising the clean-up leg changes only which sentence the author reads; it admits nothing.

**must-fix** — none.

**should-fix** — none.

**nit**

- **N3.** The flow description states the referenced-record delete; the hook `runAs` and action `body` descriptions do not, though the same refusal reaches them. Row 25 and the changeset cover all three.
- **N4.** Only the reference-clearing leg gets the delete-worded answer. A ledger whose reference was authored to delete with its parent is still refused, but with the direct-write wording. No shipped ledger declares one.
- **N2** carried over.
